Tasks: 36 SlopCodeBench problems, Python track. Configurations: 15 models in native harnesses (just-solve), plus harness variants (OpenCode, Claude Code for open models) and prompt variants (anti-slop, plan-first) on GPT 5.3 Codex, 5.4, 5.5. Baselines: just-solve prompt for the prompting study; human repository panel (473 repos) as calibration for quality. Held constant: problems and hidden tests, Docker image and tooling baseline, 2-hour limit, no turn or cost cap, reasoning effort high (none for Composer 2 and some OpenCode runs); harness version differs per model (earliest compatible). Acceptance tests: hidden tests (core, error, functionality, regression). Repetitions: not stated; one run per configuration reported. Human intervention: none

No configuration solves any problem end to end; best strict solve rate GPT 5.5 14.8% (iso 28.1%). Core pass rate falls from 64.6% to 35.5% across progress while cost per checkpoint grows 2.2x. Erosion rises in 77% and verbosity in 75.5% of trajectories; functions with CC >= 10 from 3.6 to 23.7. Agent code 2.3x more verbose (0.44 vs 0.19) and 2.0x more eroded (0.68 vs 0.34) than human repositories; per-checkpoint slopes 0.0144/0.0264 vs human 0.0022/0.0053. Anti-slop lowers verbosity 27.5-35.6% and erosion 34.3-57.6% on GPT models but not the degradation slope; prompts lower strict solve by 2.4 pp (anti-slop) and 3.6 pp (plan-first) and raise cost per checkpoint by 12.1% on average. No hypothesis tests; SDs and 95% CIs (Figure 4) only

Distinguished models (strict 1.5-14.8%) and exposed quality degradation invisible to pass rates; erosion metric stable across nine threshold/size variants (near-zero correlation with next-checkpoint pass rate, positive with cost). Repeatability not assessed (no repeated runs reported). Authors evaluate Python only due to cost

No limitations or threats-to-validity section. Stated: only the Python track evaluated due to cost; human panel may include post-2022 LLM-assisted commits (checked, small shift). Gaps: agents degrade code under iteration; prompting improves initial quality but cannot stop erosion; existing benchmarks are single-shot
